claims.claim: Socrates born c. 470/469 BC in Alopece; died 399 BC aged about 70.
claims.source: Plato, Apology 17d ('more than seventy'); Diogenes Laertius II.18, 44; Apollodorus via DL.

claims.claim: Father Sophroniscus a stonemason/sculptor; mother Phaenarete a midwife.
claims.source: Diogenes Laertius II.18 (Yonge: 'statuary'); Plato, Theaetetus 149a.

claims.claim: Wife Xanthippe, three sons.
claims.source: Plato, Phaedo 60a, 116b; Apology 34d; DL II.26.

claims.claim: Served at Potidaea, Amphipolis and Delium; saved Alcibiades at Potidaea; calm in the retreat from Delium.
claims.source: Plato, Apology 28e; Symposium 219e–221b; Laches 181b.

claims.claim: Ugly: snub nose, bulging eyes; went barefoot.
claims.source: Plato, Symposium 215a–b, 220b; Theaetetus 143e; Xenophon, Symposium 5.

claims.claim: Cicero: Socrates first brought philosophy down from the heavens into cities, to examine life and morals.
claims.source: Cicero, Tusculan Disputations V.4.10, tr. C. D. Yonge (Gutenberg #14988), checked in cached text.

claims.claim: Parthenon built 447–432 BC.
claims.source: Standard: construction 447–438, sculpture to 432 BC.

claims.claim: Peloponnesian War 431–404; plague from 430 killed perhaps a quarter; Sicilian disaster 413; surrender 404.
claims.source: Thucydides II.47–54, VII; Xenophon, Hellenica II.2. 'A quarter' is a common modern estimate: PLEASE CHECK wording.

claims.claim: The Thirty killed about 1,500 Athenians; amnesty of 403 BC.
claims.source: Aristotle, Athenian Constitution 35.4; 39–40; Xenophon, Hellenica II.4.43.

claims.claim: Arginusae 406 BC: Socrates, presiding, refused to put the illegal collective vote; there were eight generals (Xenophon writes 'nine' in Memorabilia).
claims.source: Xenophon, Memorabilia I.1.18; Hellenica I.7; Plato, Apology 32b–c.

claims.claim: Socrates refused the Thirty's order to arrest Leon of Salamis.
claims.source: Plato, Apology 32c–d.

claims.claim: The Clouds staged 423 BC at the City Dionysia, placed third; surviving text a partial revision (c. 418–416 BC) not performed.
claims.source: Hypotheses to the Clouds; Clouds 518–562 (parabasis). Standard (K. J. Dover, Clouds, 1968).

claims.claim: Socrates quotes the Clouds' 'walks in air' at his trial.
claims.source: Plato, Apology 19c.

claims.claim: Plato names himself in Apology 34a, 38b and Phaedo 59b only.
claims.source: Standard observation; PLEASE CHECK 'only three times'.

claims.claim: Phaedrus 274c–277a: the myth of Theuth; writing cannot answer questions.
claims.source: Plato, Phaedrus 274c–277a.

claims.claim: Vlastos's view that the early dialogues show the historical Socrates; Kahn's doubts.
claims.source: G. Vlastos, Socrates: Ironist and Moral Philosopher (1991); C. Kahn, Plato and the Socratic Dialogue (1996).

claims.claim: Aristotle distinguishes Socrates (definitions, virtues) from Plato (separate forms).
claims.source: Aristotle, Metaphysics I.6 987b1–10; XIII.4 1078b17–32.

claims.claim: Xenophon's version of the oracle: no one more free, just or sensible.
claims.source: Xenophon, Apology of Socrates 14.

claims.claim: Croesus and the oracle.
claims.source: Herodotus I.53, 91.

claims.claim: 'Know thyself' inscribed at Delphi, among sayings attributed to the Seven Sages.
claims.source: Pausanias X.24.1; Plato, Protagoras 343a–b; Charmides 164d; Phaedrus 229e.

claims.claim: 'I know that I know nothing' is not verbatim in Plato; Apology 21d reads 'I neither know nor think that I know' (Jowett).
claims.source: Checked in Gutenberg #1656; the Latin 'scio me nihil scire' is a later summary (cf. Cicero, Academica I.16).

claims.claim: Socrates claims to know that disobeying a better is evil.
claims.source: Apology 29b.

claims.claim: Thrasymachus complains of Socrates' 'customary irony'.
claims.source: Plato, Republic I.337a.

claims.claim: Augustine: 'a great question to myself'.
claims.source: Confessions IV.4.9 ('factus eram ipse mihi magna quaestio').

claims.claim: Kruger and Dunning 1999; later critiques argue part of the effect is statistical artefact.
claims.source: J. Kruger & D. Dunning, JPSP 77(6) (1999) 1121–1134; E. Nuhfer et al., Numeracy 9(1) (2016). PLEASE CHECK the critique citation.

claims.claim: Xenophon's argument from design.
claims.source: Memorabilia I.4.5–7.

claims.claim: Euthyphro 6a: Socrates finds stories of quarrelling gods hard to accept.
claims.source: Plato, Euthyphro 6a–c.

claims.claim: Meno: Thessalian aristocrat, pupil of Gorgias; later a treacherous general in Cyrus' expedition; dialogue set c. 402 BC.
claims.source: Plato, Meno 70a–b, 76b; Xenophon, Anabasis II.6.21–29. Dramatic date conventional.

claims.claim: Anytus warns Socrates in the Meno (94e).
claims.source: Plato, Meno 94e, Jowett text checked in #1643.

claims.claim: Meno 99e–100b: virtue by divine dispensation, not teaching.
claims.source: Plato, Meno 99e–100b.

claims.claim: Vlastos's analysis of the elenchus and 'the problem of the elenchus'.
claims.source: G. Vlastos, 'The Socratic Elenchus', OSAP 1 (1983) 27–58.

claims.claim: Gorgias: Socrates tells Polus/Callicles they really believe doing wrong is worse.
claims.source: Plato, Gorgias 474b, 482b.

claims.claim: Socrates' midwifery.
claims.source: Plato, Theaetetus 150b–c.

claims.claim: Augustine, De Magistro (389) with Adeodatus: Christ the inner teacher; De Trinitate XII.15.24 criticises the Meno's recollection.
claims.source: Augustine, De Magistro 11.38–12.40; De Trinitate XII.15.24.

claims.claim: Langdell introduced the case method at Harvard Law in the 1870s; Beck's cognitive therapy uses Socratic questioning.
claims.source: B. A. Kimball, The Inception of Modern Professional Education (2009); A. T. Beck, Cognitive Therapy and the Emotional Disorders (1976).

claims.claim: Indictment wording preserved, per Favorinus, in the Metroon.
claims.source: Diogenes Laertius II.40 (Yonge, #57342, checked); the Metroon was the record office (Yonge: 'temple of Cybele').

claims.claim: Graphē asebeias lodged with the king archon; jury of about 500 (501) over thirty, chosen by lot; water clock; no deliberation.
claims.source: Plato, Euthyphro 2a; Aristotle, Athenian Constitution 57, 63–69.

claims.claim: Vote about 280 to 220 (thirty votes would have acquitted).
claims.source: Plato, Apology 36a; DL II.41 gives a confused figure (281; 'six more').

claims.claim: Penalty: free meals in the Prytaneum, then one mina, then thirty minae guaranteed by Plato, Crito, Critobulus, Apollodorus; death by eighty more votes.
claims.source: Apology 36d–38b; DL II.42.

claims.claim: Xenophon says Socrates chose not to defend himself fully, thinking it time to die.
claims.source: Xenophon, Apology of Socrates 1–9; Memorabilia IV.8.

claims.claim: Aeschines: 'you put to death Socrates the sophist, because he was shown to have educated Critias'.
claims.source: Aeschines, Against Timarchus 173 (345 BC). Quoted in our own wording of the common English rendering: PLEASE CHECK against a PD translation or mark as paraphrase.

claims.claim: Herms and Mysteries scandal of 415 BC; Alcibiades condemned.
claims.source: Thucydides VI.27–29, 53, 60–61.

claims.claim: Daimonion: from childhood; only forbids (Plato); Xenophon says it also advised; did not oppose him on the day of the trial.
claims.source: Apology 31c–d, 40a–c; Xenophon, Memorabilia I.1.4.

claims.claim: Plutarch's On the Sign of Socrates.
claims.source: Plutarch, De genio Socratis, esp. 588c–589f.

claims.claim: Jury pay three obols.
claims.source: Aristotle, Athenian Constitution 62.2; Aristophanes, Wasps.

claims.claim: Mina ≈ 100 drachmas ≈ 100 days' wages of a skilled worker.
claims.source: Erechtheum building accounts (409–406 BC): 1 drachma a day.

claims.claim: Delian ship: about thirty days.
claims.source: Xenophon, Memorabilia IV.8.2; Plato, Phaedo 58a–c.

claims.claim: Crito's plan; Simmias and Cebes brought money; friends in Thessaly.
claims.source: Plato, Crito 44b–46a.

claims.claim: Locke's tacit consent; Hume's peasant and the ship.
claims.source: Locke, Second Treatise §119–122; Hume, 'Of the Original Contract' (1748).

claims.claim: Thoreau jailed 1846, essay 1849; King's Letter (1963) names Socrates.
claims.source: Thoreau, 'Resistance to Civil Government' (1849); King, 'Letter from Birmingham Jail' (1963).

claims.claim: Calvin on lesser magistrates.
claims.source: Calvin, Institutes IV.20.31–32.

claims.claim: Kraut: 'persuade or obey' allows open disobedience.
claims.source: R. Kraut, Socrates and the State (1984).

claims.claim: Socrates in prison composed verses and a hymn to Apollo because of a dream.
claims.source: Plato, Phaedo 60e–61b.

claims.claim: Thessaly 'great disorder and licence'.
claims.source: Crito 53d, Jowett text checked.

claims.claim: Alcibiades c. 450–404, ward of Pericles, Sicilian expedition, defection; Critias c. 460–403 leader of the Thirty, killed 403 with Charmides.
claims.source: Thucydides VI; Plutarch, Alcibiades; Xenophon, Hellenica II.3–4.

claims.claim: Sicilian disaster cost perhaps 40,000 men.
claims.source: Thucydides VII.75 (40,000 in the retreat, including non-combatants). PLEASE CHECK wording.

claims.claim: Oligarchic coups 411 (Four Hundred), 404 (Thirty), 401 (Eleusis).
claims.source: Thucydides VIII; Aristotle, Athenian Constitution 29–33, 40.4; Xenophon, Hellenica II.4.43.

claims.claim: Polycrates' Accusation of Socrates c. 393 BC, answered by Xenophon's 'accuser'.
claims.source: DL II.39 (Favorinus on the Conon anachronism); scholarly consensus (e.g. Dorion).

claims.claim: I. F. Stone's argument: anti-democracy, free speech defence, provocation; learned Greek for the book.
claims.source: I. F. Stone, The Trial of Socrates (1988). Summarised in our own words: PLEASE CHECK the 401 BC point is Stone's emphasis.

claims.claim: Hegel: Socrates' fate tragic, two rights; Athens justified by its law and repented.
claims.source: Hegel, Lectures on the History of Philosophy I (Haldane, 1892), 'Fate of Socrates'. Our own words.

claims.claim: Nietzsche: Birth of Tragedy on theoretical man; Twilight 'The Problem of Socrates' on ugliness, dialectic as revenge, reason as tyrant, last words, wanting to die; 'Platonism for the people'.
claims.source: Nietzsche, BT §§12–15; TI 'Problem of Socrates' 1–12; GS §340; Beyond Good and Evil, Preface ('Platonism for the people'). Our own words; no translation quoted.

claims.claim: Mill on Socrates and Calvary.
claims.source: On Liberty ch. II (Gutenberg #34901), quoted verbatim.

claims.claim: Plato's warning about young people and argument (puppies).
claims.source: Republic VII.537e–539d.

claims.claim: Phaedo narrated by Phaedo of Elis to Echecrates at Phlius; Phaedo a former slave freed by Socrates' friends.
claims.source: Phaedo 57a; DL II.105. PLEASE CHECK the freeing story (sources vary on who ransomed him).

claims.claim: Hemlock not named by Plato.
claims.source: Phaedo 117a ('the poison'); later sources name hemlock (koneion).

claims.claim: Justin Martyr: philosopher from Samaria (Flavia Neapolis), wore the philosopher's cloak, beheaded in Rome c. 165.
claims.source: Justin, Dialogue with Trypho 1–8; Eusebius, Church History IV.11, 16; Acts of Justin.

claims.claim: Justin quotes Timaeus 28c.
claims.source: Second Apology 10; Plato, Timaeus 28c.

claims.claim: Justin, First Apology 46: those who lived with the Word, like Socrates and Heraclitus, are Christians.
claims.source: First Apology 46 (mentioned only: reserved as a reading for When Athens met Jerusalem).

claims.claim: Clement: philosophy a schoolmaster to Christ.
claims.source: Stromata I.5.

claims.claim: Erasmus, Convivium religiosum (1522): 'Sancte Socrates, ora pro nobis'.
claims.source: Erasmus, Colloquies, 'The Godly Feast'.

claims.claim: Rousseau's sage/God comparison.
claims.source: Emile (1762), Book IV, Profession of Faith of the Savoyard Vicar.

claims.claim: Cullmann's 1955 Ingersoll Lecture.
claims.source: O. Cullmann, Immortality of the Soul or Resurrection of the Dead? (1958 English).

claims.claim: Glenn Most on the cock for Asclepius (Plato's recovery).
claims.source: G. W. Most, 'A Cock for Asclepius', Classical Quarterly 43 (1993) 96–111. PLEASE CHECK.

claims.claim: Rule of Benedict ch. 4: keep death daily before one's eyes.
claims.source: RB 4.47 (paraphrased, not quoted).

claims.claim: Music: Messiaen composed the Quartet in Stalag VIII-A, premiered 15 January 1941; Vaughan Williams edited The English Hymnal (1906), Tallis's tune from Parker's Psalter (1567), RVW agnostic; Fauré on death as 'happy deliverance'.
claims.source: Standard music histories; Fauré interview (1902) with Louis Aguettant/ in Jean-Michel Nectoux, Fauré (1991). PLEASE CHECK Fauré wording and RVW 'agnostic' phrasing.

claims.claim: Be Thou My Vision: translated by Mary Byrne (1905) and versified by Eleanor Hull (1912); line 'Be Thou my Wisdom, and Thou my true Word'.
claims.source: Hull d. 1935 (public domain). content/music.json note.

claims.claim: Romans 13 written c. AD 57 under Nero; 1 Corinthians c. AD 54; Daniel's final form 160s BC under Antiochus IV.
claims.source: Standard introductions (e.g. Oxford Bible Commentary).

claims.claim: Kierkegaard: Christ is not a teacher like Socrates.
claims.source: Kierkegaard, Philosophical Fragments (1844), ch. I.

claims.claim: Mogens Hansen: Socrates probably guilty by Athenian standards.
claims.source: M. H. Hansen, The Trial of Sokrates: from the Athenian Point of View (1995). PLEASE CHECK.

claims.claim: Regnault, Socrates Dragging Alcibiades from the Embrace of Sensual Pleasure (1791), not at NGA; David's Death of Socrates (1787) at the Met.
claims.source: Louvre (Regnault); Metropolitan Museum 31.45.
